decisions.question: e-6629

source.question: e-6629
source.value:
Find the general solution to the equation

$$
x^2 y'' + xy' + 4y = 0,\quad x > 0.
$$

decisions.reason: Observed MA content supersedes the stored value

decisions.question: e-6629

source.question: e-6629
source.value:
This is an instance of the Cauchy-Euler equation. So, we assume the solutions take the form $y=x^\lambda.$ Differentiating $y$ with respect to $x$ gives

$$
y' = \lambda x^{\lambda -1}, \qquad y'' = \lambda(\lambda-1)x^{\lambda-2}
$$

Substituting the above to our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}\cdot \lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda -2}+x\cdot \lambda {x}^{\lambda -1}+4{x}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ \lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda }+\lambda {x}^{\lambda }+4{x}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ {x}^{\lambda }[\lambda (\lambda -1)+\lambda +4] & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following characteristic equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda (\lambda -1)+\lambda +4 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}+4 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2} & =-4 \\ \lambda  & =\pm 2\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
y(x)=c_1 \cos( 2 \ln{x} )  + c_2\sin( 2 \ln{x} ).
$$

$$

decisions.question: e-6630

source.question: e-6630
source.value:
This is an instance of the Cauchy-Euler equation. So, we assume the solutions take the form $y=t^\lambda.$ Differentiating $y$ with respect to $t$ gives

$$
y' = \lambda t^{\lambda -1}, \qquad y'' = \lambda(\lambda-1)t^{\lambda-2}.
$$

Substituting the above to our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2}\cdot \lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda -2}+5t\cdot \lambda {t}^{\lambda -1}+8{t}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ \lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda }+5\lambda {t}^{\lambda }+8{t}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ {t}^{\lambda }[\lambda (\lambda -1)+5\lambda +8] & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following characteristic equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda (\lambda -1)+5\lambda +8 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}+4\lambda +8 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

We solve the auxiliary equation by completing the square:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}+4\lambda +8 & =0 \\ ({\lambda }^{2}+4\lambda +4)-4+8 & =0 \\ (\lambda +2)^{2} & =-4 \\ \lambda +2 & =\pm 2\text{i} \\ \lambda  & =-2\pm 2\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
y(t) = t^{-2} \left( c_1 \cos( 2 \ln{t} ) + c_2 \sin( 2 \ln{t} ) \right).
$$

decisions.question: e-6631

source.question: e-6631
source.value:
Given that the differential equation

$$
x^2 y'' + xy' + 49 y = 0
$$

has the general solution

$$
y(x)= c_1 \cos(7 \ln{x} )  + c_2\sin(7 \ln{x} ),
$$

solve the initial value problem

$$
x^2 y'' + xy' + 49 y = 0, \quad y(1) = 0, \quad y'(1) = -7, \quad x > 0.
$$

decisions.question: e-6631

source.question: e-6631
source.value:
We find the constants $c_1$ and $c_2$ using the initial conditions.

- Substituting $y(1) = 0$ into the general solution gives

$$
0 = c_1.
$$

- To apply the condition $y'(1) = -7,$ we first differentiate $y$ to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =\frac{7}{x}({c}_{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(7\operatorname{ln}⁡x)-{c}_{1}\operatorname{sin}⁡(7\operatorname{ln}⁡x)).\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $y'(1) = -7$ and $c_1 = 0$ into the above to get

$$
\begin{aligned}-7 & =7{c}_{2} \\ {c}_{2} & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
y(x) = -\sin(7 \ln{x} ).
$$

source.value:
We find the constants $c_1$ and $c_2$ using the initial conditions.

- To apply the condition $y'(1) = -1,$ we first differentiate $y$ to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & ={c}_{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\operatorname{ln}⁡t)+3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\operatorname{ln}⁡t)).\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $y'(1) = -1$ and $c_1=0$ into the above to get

$$
\begin{aligned}-1 & =3{c}_{2} \\ -\frac{1}{3} & ={c}_{2}.\end{aligned}

$$
y(t) = -\dfrac{ t\sin( 3 \ln{t}) )}{3}.
